Hi Lisa (and PayWise security team),

Thanks again for taking the call earlier - great to meet you all. Per our discussion, wanted to summarize the key encryption points and next steps so your security team has a clear view:

High-level summary:
- In-transit: All customer traffic to Redwood endpoints is TLS 1.2+ (we recommend 1.3). We provide mTLS for dedicated/private deployments on request.
- At-rest: Model artifacts and cached data are encrypted at rest using AES-256. Our hosted control plane stores metadata encrypted; customer data stored in serving nodes is encrypted with keys managed via our KMS integration.
- Customer-managed keys (CMK/KMS/HSM): Redwood supports bringing your own key via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted accounts we offer a BYOK option for enterprise customers with a dedicated key ring and granular access controls. We can also integrate with customer HSMs for on-prem Private installs.
- Logging & retention: We can limit request/response logging for routes that handle PII. By default we retain request logs for 30 days; retention policy can be customized under enterprise agreements. Audit logs (auth events, key rotations) can be exported to your SIEM.

Attachments: I've attached a short KMS overview PDF and a diagram that maps data flows to key boundaries.

Next steps / action items:
1) Lisa / Security: share your completed security questionnaire (I see you flagged some KMS-related Qs) - I attached the questionnaire template for convenience.
2) Redwood: Dev will provide a short implementation write-up covering KMS key policies, rotation, and HSM support.
3) Schedule: propose a 30-minute technical deep-dive next week with your infra/security leads and our solutions engineer.

If it helps, we can also prepare an architecture diagram showing how keys are scoped for multi-tenant hosted vs dedicated lanes.

Thanks - talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa - helpful recap. A few clarifying points from our side after an initial pass:

1) BYOK for hosted: can you confirm whether your hosted BYOK option ensures that Redwood never has access to the plaintext keys? Are keys material ever exported to your control plane?
2) Key rotation: what is the typical rotation process and downtime impact? Do you support staggered rotation and key versioning so old tokens still validate for a transition window?
3) HSM / FIPS: we're required to use FIPS 140-2 validated HSMs for certain PII workloads. Do you have references for HSM integrations (on-prem or cloud) and any attestation docs?
4) Logging PII: can you confirm whether request/response payloads containing PII can be fully disabled from logging at the route-level? We need to be able to show evidence to auditors.

I'm attaching our security questionnaire (partially filled). The security team would like short answers we can include in the questionnaire and any supporting artifact links. Also please include any SOC 2 / penetration test reports we can share under NDA.

Our security lead (security@paywise.com) might follow up with a few technical folks. Would be great if Dev or your solutions engineer could respond to the KMS-specific questions.

Thanks,
Lisa
Sr. Security Engineer | PayWise
lisa.cheng@paywise.com

Hi Lisa - quick technical answers below (happy to expand in the deep-dive):

1) BYOK for hosted: Keys are customer-owned and stored in your cloud KMS (we leverage envelope encryption). Redwood never persists your plaintext key material. For hosted BYOK we request a wrapped key or authorize Redwood's service principal to use your KMS key; key material never leaves your KMS.

2) Key rotation: We support key versioning and staggered rotations. Typical approach: create new key version in your KMS, update Redwood's configuration to point to the new key version, and continue to accept tokens encrypted with the old key for a configurable grace period (we recommend 7 days). No service downtime required - we hot-swap key references and re-encrypt cached artifacts asynchronously.

3) HSM / FIPS: For Dedicated and Private deployments we integrate directly with customer HSMs or cloud HSM-backed KMS (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM). We can provide FIPS attestations and customer references under NDA - I'll loop in our compliance docs.

4) Logging PII: Route-level logging controls exist. We can configure filters to drop or redact request/response payloads containing PII before they reach long-term logs. For hosted customers we also offer a private tenancy option where logging can be fully disabled and audit events exported only to the customer's syslog/S3 endpoints.

Additional notes:
- Audit logs: we expose key usage audit events and rotate access keys on a schedule. Exports to your SIEM via secure forwarders are supported.
- KMS policies: we recommend using least-privilege IAM roles with condition-based access (source IP, time windows) for Redwood service principals when granting decrypt/encrypt permissions.

Happy to prepare short answers for the questionnaire items you attached - Marissa, want me to fill the spreadsheet and send back?

Thanks,
